transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Since I watched that car get crushed in front of me last week, I’ve gone out of my way to avoid driving or even being near busy intersections. A pickup truck ran a red light and flipped the car right in front of me, and I've just been terrified of getting behind the wheel or crossing busy streets since then.
Besides avoiding driving, are you also experiencing vivid, unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the accident?

Yes, I am. Out of nowhere, even when I'm just making coffee or looking at spreadsheets, the image of that car flipping flashes in my mind and my chest clamps up like I'm right back there. At night, I lie awake for hours replaying the crash over and over instead of sleeping.
Since the accident happened last week, have these flashbacks, avoidance, and sleep issues been constant every day, or have they started to lessen in intensity?
They have been constant every single day since the accident, and they haven't lessened in intensity at all. It feels like it's happening non-stop, and I'm just completely exhausted.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge, unusually jumpy, or easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I've been incredibly jumpy and on edge. Even a door closing or someone walking up behind me makes me jump out of my skin, and my heart will pound for minutes afterward before I can calm down. Even at night, I find myself jerking awake at the slightest little sound.
To help me understand the timeline better, has it been less than a month since the accident occurred, or has it been longer than that?
It’s been much less than a month—the accident actually happened just last week. All of these feelings started immediately after the crash and have been going on constantly since then.
Since the accident, have you experienced times where you felt detached from your own body, or did your surroundings seem dreamlike and unreal?

No, I haven't really felt detached from my body or like my surroundings are dreamlike or unreal. Everything actually feels way too real and overwhelming, especially when I'm trying to avoid those busy streets.
Have you ever experienced a similar traumatic event in your past that caused these kinds of symptoms, or is this the very first time you've felt this way?
No, I have never experienced a traumatic event like this before. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way, and these symptoms are completely new to me.
How have these symptoms, like the avoidance and being constantly on edge, affected your ability to work or manage your daily responsibilities?

It’s been incredibly disruptive; I’ve been leaving work early, missing deadlines, and making mistakes on my spreadsheets that my manager actually noticed. I’ve also had to cancel my high-school mentoring sessions and skip my running club because I just can't bring myself to drive or go near busy intersections.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with characteristic symptoms of post-traumatic stress following a qualifying traumatic event (witnessing a severe car accident). These include intrusive memories (flashbacks and replaying the event), active avoidance of trauma-related stimuli (driving and busy intersections), and marked hyperarousal (being constantly on edge and easily startled). Although the symptoms have only persisted for one week (which typically meets the timeframe for Acute Stress Reaction, F43.0), the clinical presentation strongly aligns with the symptom profile of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1).
